clue.text: Snappy son with little yen to show gesture of respect

parts.note: a snappy reply is curt, short and sharp
Y is the abbreviation (a 'little' version) of the Japanese currency yen

explanation.surface: A curt young man with a little Japanese money bows politely to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsy is the bob made by bending the knees, a traditional mark of deference.

clue.text: Wood that may be all-too familiar

definitions.meaning: a stale joke or story heard too often

explanation.surface: A tree whose name might be tiresomely well known.
explanation.definitionFit: Chestnut names both a hardwood tree and an old, over-told joke that everyone already knows.

clue.text: Prepared to study, getting to university finally

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word university

explanation.surface: A student primed to study, eventually making it to university.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready means set or equipped to act, the same sense as prepared.

clue.text: Newcomer in Yorkshire location overlooking river

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooking puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: Settle is a market town in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A new arrival in a Yorkshire town with a view of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is someone who arrives to make a home in a new place, a newcomer.

clue.text: Tries to be reverse of good person meeting office worker?

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

indicators.note: reverse of tells us to read the letters for the good person backwards

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to be the opposite of a saint by flirting with a colleague at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to try or test them, as in the biblical sense of putting a person to the test.

clue.text: Get on with any number in English school

indicators.note: in puts the number's letter inside the English school letters

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: Advice to get along with the pupils at an English school.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a train, so it means to get on one.

clue.text: Receiver of gift now beginning to enthuse repeatedly

parts.note: the present is now, the current time

indicators.note: repeatedly means that letter is used twice in a row
the beginning of the word enthuse is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone opening a present starts gushing again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to enthuse' gives E and 'repeatedly' doubles it to EE.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentee is the person to whom something is presented, the recipient of a present.

clue.text: Seat is adjusted for forty winks?

indicators.note: adjusted means altered or rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A chair is reclined so someone can take a quick nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty winks is a short nap, and a siesta is a nap taken in the afternoon.

clue.text: Margaret when meeting sailor is a dazzling personality

parts.note: Meg is a short form of the name Margaret
as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A woman named Margaret, out with a seaman, turns out to be a glittering celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastar is an exceptionally famous performer, a celebrity whose fame outshines ordinary stars.

clue.text: Gnarled sire out with leading crooks?

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order, jumbled

explanation.surface: A wizened old father turns up alongside the heads of a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringleaders are those who lead a gang of wrongdoers, so they are the chief crooks.

clue.text: Break them and content damns me?

definitions.text: Break them and content damns me?

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it apart, so the letters of the words after it are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sinner muses that breaking the rules, though satisfying, will be their damnation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' signals an anagram of THEM CONTENT DAMNS ME. The whole clue also describes the answer: breaking the commandments damns the sinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ten Commandments are the biblical laws given to Moses; breaking them is sin that brings damnation.

clue.text: Don't go to offer support

definitions.meaning: a prop or brace that supports something, such as a mast

explanation.surface: A plea to someone not to leave, offering them help.
explanation.definitionFit: Stay is both the verb for remaining where you are and a noun for a rope or prop holding up a mast.

clue.text: Property managers come down — are primarily good guys?

parts.note: to land is to come down to earth

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the first letter of the word are is used

parts.note: gents, short for gentlemen, are good, decent guys

explanation.surface: Estate managers arrive and are essentially decent fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: Land agents manage estates on behalf of owners, collecting rents and running the property.

clue.text: Betty felt urn could become insect container

indicators.note: could become says these letters may be turned into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: Betty thinks an urn might be turned into a box for keeping bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfly net is a mesh bag on a pole used to catch and hold insects.

clue.text: Catch with line configured like a sort of hitch?

indicators.note: configured means set up in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A knot tied from a fishing catch and line, like a hitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical hitch is a mechanical or equipment fault, so the answer describes that kind of hitch.

clue.text: Head of school, teaser and martinet?

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the word school

parts.note: a tickler is a puzzle or teaser, as in brain-tickler

explanation.surface: A headmaster who sets puzzles and is a strict disciplinarian.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet insists on strict discipline, and a stickler insists on rules being followed exactly.

clue.text: See 10
Some art slammed by this expert practitioner?

indicators.note: slammed means violently knocked about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An art expert pans an exhibition in a scathing review.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master of an art, especially a distinguished conductor or musician.

clue.text: Stylish dog with no tail outside wood

indicators.note: outside says the shortened dog goes around the wood
with no tail removes the last letter of the dog

parts.note: the dingo is the wild dog of Australia
ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A smart-looking dog with a docked tail is out in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing describes someone attractive and smartly turned out, which is stylish.

clue.text: Yarn — what runs through it for reader?

definitions.text: what runs through it for reader?
definitions.meaning: the ... of a story is the line of argument or plot a reader follows through it

explanation.surface: A tale, and the line that carries a reader through it.
explanation.walkthrough: Yarn is both spun fibre and a story, and the second definition plays on the story sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Thread is spun fibre, and also the connecting plot line running through a narrative.

clue.text: Eternal message of conservative folk?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the phrase ... is what conservatives urge

explanation.surface: An everlasting slogan from people who resist reform.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into CHANGE LESS, the instruction a conservative would give.
explanation.definitionFit: Something changeless never varies, so it is everlasting in the sense of permanent.

clue.text: The old man going to court to secure agreement

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, the old man

explanation.surface: Dad heads to court to obtain a settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal deal or treaty between parties.

clue.text: Material for party in Wales?

definitions.meaning: ... Cymru, often just ..., is the Welsh nationalist political party

explanation.surface: Which fabric to wear for a celebration in Wales?
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is a checked tartan cloth and also the short name of Wales's nationalist party.

clue.text: Officer in race? He's a cool guy

indicators.note: in says the officer's letters sit inside the race's letters

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying race
PC is the abbreviation for police constable, a British police officer

explanation.surface: A policeman taking part in a race is admired as a cool customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepcat is old jazz slang for a hip, stylish person.

clue.text: It's appropriate to have one American brought back on board

indicators.note: brought back says these letters are returned the other way round

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a board can be a table, as in 'bed and board'

explanation.surface: Bringing an American back to join the board seems fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses USI (American plus one) to make SUI, which goes on TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitable means fitting or right for the purpose, a synonym of appropriate.

clue.text: Model needing work? Just a bit

parts.note: a doll is a model of a person
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A model needs a job, but only a little one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a small shapeless lump or portion of something soft, such as cream.

clue.text: African city tribe in broadcast

indicators.note: in places the tribe's letters inside those of the broadcast

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: A people featured in a broadcast programme about Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a port and resort city on the Atlantic coast of Morocco.
